newsitem.title: CANADA: British Columbia lumber talks recess for week.
newsitem.headline: British Columbia lumber talks recess for week.

text.p: Negotiators for British Columbia's coastal lumber companies and their unionized workers met briefly on Wednesday and decided to reconvene next week, a union spokesman said.
The IWA-Canada union had hoped to receive a contract proposal from Forest Industrial Relations which represents the companies.
But a union spokesman said the companies instead used the meeting to request clarification of various points and then asked for talks to be held over until Monday.
At that meeting, the companies are expected to present an economic analysis on industry costs and performance, he said.

The union believes the companies may want to wait until after the British Columbia government announces Thursday initiatives aimed at increasing employment in the sector by 21,000 jobs over the next four years.
Part of that agreement is expected to include provisions encouraging workers to refuse overtime as a way of prodding companies to expand their payrolls.
The union's previous contract expired last Saturday and the union has said it may consider taking a strike vote in early July if talks have not made sufficient progress by then.
